sentences.15.2 «Jeg vil vise innvandrerkvinner at: 15.2 "I want to show immigrant women that anything is possible!"
sentences.Hvis du tar bussen i Oslo, får du kanskj: If you take the bus in Oslo, you might get Aisha as your driver.
sentences.Aisha var den første somaliske kvinnen s: Aisha was the first Somali woman to get a bus driver's licence in Oslo.
sentences.Nå håper hun at enda flere innvandrerkvi: Now she hopes that even more immigrant women will dare to follow their dreams.
sentences.Hvorfor ble du bussjåfør?: Why did you become a bus driver?
sentences.Jeg har hatt mange jobber i Norge, men j: I have had lots of jobs in Norway, but I have always dreamed of driving a bus or becoming a pilot.
sentences.Det var ikke mulig da jeg vokste opp i M: That wasn't possible when I grew up in Mogadishu, because there only men could have jobs like that.
sentences.Her i Norge er alt mulig, også for kvinn: Here in Norway anything is possible, for women too.
sentences.Dattera mi skal få lov til å gjøre hva h: My daughter will be allowed to do whatever she wants.
sentences.Hvordan er det å være en muslimsk kvinne: What is it like to be a Muslim woman who drives a bus?
sentences.Mange smiler og snakker med meg, men noe: Many people smile and talk to me, but some Norwegians think I'm a Muslim extremist because I wear a hijab, and say that "people like me" shouldn't drive buses.
sentences.Noen muslimer sier til meg at jeg er en: Some Muslims tell me that I am a bad Muslim because I wear trousers and drive a bus.
sentences.Jeg blir ikke en bedre muslim hvis jeg i: I don't become a better Muslim if I don't wear trousers or don't work.
Your Norwegian has become very good.
sentences.Har du noen tips til nye innvandrere?: Do you have any tips for new immigrants?
sentences.Ja, du må være sosial, gå på kaféer og b: Yes, you have to be sociable, go to cafés and use women's groups or other international groups in your municipality.
You have to seek out places where things are happening.
sentences.Til innvandrerkvinner vil jeg si: Ikke s: To immigrant women I would say: Don't sit at home!
You have to work and be sociable.
sentences.Det er ingen framtid å sitte hjemme med: There's no future in sitting at home with the children. At work you learn lots of new words that you don't learn at school.
sentences.Jeg har lært å snakke norsk gjennom jobb: I have learned to speak Norwegian through the jobs I have had.
sentences.Jeg har jobbet både som renholder, hjemm: I have worked as a cleaner, a home help, a mother-tongue assistant, an interpreter and in a nursery.
sentences.Har du begynt å gjøre noen typisk norske: Have you started doing any typically Norwegian things?
sentences.Ja, det er mange ting, men jeg vil si at: Yes, there are lots of things, but I would say that I have learned a lot here.
sentences.Jeg har lært at det er viktig å møte pre: I have learned that it is important to be on time, and I have learned to say no if I can't do something.
sentences.I begynnelsen tenkte jeg at det var uhøf: At first I thought it was rude to say no, but I have understood that it is really important.
sentences.Hvis du ikke kan eller ikke forstår, må: If you can't or don't understand, you mustn't say yes!
sentences.Hva kan innvandrere gjøre for å bli kjen: What can immigrants do to get to know Norwegians?
You just have to contribute to society.
sentences.Hvis du er med på dugnader og arrangemen: If you take part in dugnads and events, you get to know Norwegians.
sentences.De fleste nordmenn er litt forsiktige og: Most Norwegians are a bit reserved and difficult to get in touch with.
sentences.De er ikke sure eller uinteresserte, men: They aren't grumpy or uninterested, they just ARE like that!
We immigrants have to be a bit brave.
sentences.Hvis du inviterer en nordmann på en kaff: If you invite a Norwegian for a coffee, you may get a new friend.
sentences.Den beste måten å bli kjent med nordmenn: The best way to get to know Norwegians is perhaps to invite them on a ski trip!
